question: From which of the following states / union territories does the Yamuna River originate?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttarakhand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• The Yamuna River originates from the Yamunotri Glacier, which is situated in the Uttarkashi district of Uttarakhand.

• Yamunotri is one of the four sites in India's Chota Char Dham pilgrimage.

• The river flows from the Himalayas in the north and travels a distance of about 1,376 kilometers before merging with the Ganges at the Triveni Sangam in Allahabad, Uttar Pradesh.

• The Yamuna River is the longest tributary of the Ganges and the second-largest tributary river of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Uttarakhand**

• Uttarakhand is a state in northern India crossed by the Himalayas.

• It is known for its Hindu pilgrimage sites, including Haridwar and Rishikesh, and is home to the famous Jim Corbett National Park and the Valley of Flowers National Park.

• The state is often referred to as "Devbhumi" (literally 'Land of the Gods') due to the many Hindu temples and pilgrimage centers found throughout the state.

• Uttarakhand has a diverse range of flora and fauna and is rich in natural resources, particularly water.

• **Yamunotri Glacier**

• The Yamunotri Glacier is the source of the Yamuna River, situated at an altitude of 6,387 meters above sea level in the Garhwal Himalayas.

• It is one of the primary pilgrimage sites for Hindus, with the Yamunotri Temple situated nearby.

• The glacier and temple are accessible by a trek from the town of Hanuman Chatti, which is connected by road to other parts of Uttarakhand.

• The Yamunotri region is known for its hot springs and scenic beauty, attracting tourists and devotees alike.

• **Triveni Sangam**

• The Triveni Sangam is the confluence of three rivers: the Ganges, the Yamuna, and the mythical Saraswati.

• It is considered a sacred place in Hindu tradition and is a site for the Kumbh Mela, held every twelve years.

• Bathing at the Triveni Sangam is believed to cleanse one of all sins and is a major pilgrimage destination.

• The Sangam is located in Prayagraj (formerly Allahabad) in Uttar Pradesh.
